meaning: The act of making yourself (or someone) seem less important or lower in dignity
trick: A-BASE-ment → bringing yourself down to the BASEment.
examples: She saw in his face that it had been a place of abasement and despair.
He found the constant begging a painful abasement.

usage.pattern: the abasement of someone / self-abasement

meaning: Hates something very strongly
hindi: घृणा करता है, सख्त नफरत करता है
trick: Ab-HORS-e ≈ 'bore' → he finds it so boring he hates it.
examples: A true leader abhors arrogance and never looks down on the weakest.
She abhors violence of any kind.

usage.pattern: someone abhors something / abhors doing something

meaning: To tolerate or put up with something (usually 'can't abide'); also to obey (abide by a rule)
hindi: सहन करना, बर्दाश्त करना; पालन करना
trick: Abide ≈ bride → a bride has to tolerate and obey the new family's rules.
examples: It's called getting soft, and that I could not abide.
I can't abide people who are rude to waiters.

usage.pattern: can't abide something/someone · abide by a rule/decision

meaning: Obeying or following (rules or laws); also lasting a long time
trick: Abide → abiding: always abiding by the rules.
examples: All we can do is go on abiding by the laws He has set for us.
He is a law-abiding citizen who has never broken a rule.

usage.pattern: abiding by a rule/law/decision

meaning: To officially end a law, system or practice
trick: Abolish a law → wipe it out completely.
examples: The government decided to abolish the old tax.
Many people campaigned to abolish child labour.

usage.pattern: abolish a law / system / practice

meaning: Officially ended (a law, system or practice)
trick: Abolished = to end — 'a-BOLISH-ed' → polished off for good.
examples: Remove Man from the scene, and the cause of hunger is abolished for ever.
Slavery was abolished in the British Empire in 1833.

usage.pattern: something was abolished (in + year) · someone abolished something

meaning: Sudden and unexpected; also short and slightly rude in manner
trick: 'A-BURST' → something that bursts out suddenly.
examples: She put on her jacket with the same abrupt, robot-like gestures and walked out.
The bus came to an abrupt stop.

usage.pattern: an abrupt + change/end/stop · be abrupt with someone

meaning: Declared free from blame, guilt or responsibility
trick: Absolved → the case is SOLVED, so you're no longer blamed.
examples: He agreed, but it hadn't absolved me from my sin.
The court absolved him of all charges.

usage.pattern: be absolved of/from something (blame, guilt)

meaning: To deliberately hold back from doing or enjoying something, especially voting, drinking or eating
trick: ab (away) + stain — stay away so you don't get stained.
examples: People who abstain from worldly pleasures suffer because of it.
He decided to abstain from sugar for a month.

usage.pattern: abstain from something / from doing something

meaning: Existing as an idea rather than a physical thing; not concrete
trick: Abstract art — shapes and colors, not real objects you can touch.
examples: Some problems are abstract and complicated, like finding a career you feel good about.
Love and justice are abstract ideas.

usage.pattern: an abstract + idea/concept/art

meaning: In a ridiculously unreasonable or illogical way
hindi: बेतुके ढंग से, हास्यास्पद रूप से
trick: Absurd → 'a-SURD' → like a surd number, it makes no sense.
examples: It seemed worthwhile, if absurdly so, to have endured all they had endured.
The tickets were absurdly expensive.

usage.pattern: absurdly + adjective (expensive, easy, high)

meaning: A very large quantity of something; more than enough
trick: Abundance → a BUN-dance: so many buns you could dance on them.
examples: Tapering is supposed to give you an abundance of energy as you eat and rest.
The garden had an abundance of mangoes this summer.

usage.pattern: an abundance of something · in abundance

meaning: Existing in large quantities; more than enough
trick: Abundant → a BUN-dant: buns in plenty.
examples: Does he think he will shake the abundant evidence against his client?
Fresh water is abundant in this region.

usage.pattern: something is abundant · abundant + noun

meaning: A deep, endless emptiness or nothingness that feels frightening; also a very deep pit
trick: A-BYSS ≈ 'a bottomless' pit — no bottom to be seen.
examples: Sitting on my mom's couch that summer, I stared into the abyss.
After losing his job, he felt he was falling into an abyss.

usage.pattern: stare into the abyss · fall into an abyss
partners: on the edge of the abyss

meaning: A tree or shrub with small yellow or white flowers and thorns, common in warm regions
trick: Acacia → 'a cash-ia' tree — its gum (gum arabic) used to earn cash.
examples: Babi sat at the foot of a thick-trunked acacia tree reading a paperback.
Giraffes nibble leaves from the thorny acacia.

usage.pattern: an acacia (tree) · acacia + noun

meaning: The process of getting used to a new climate or new conditions
hindi: नए माहौल का आदी होना, अनुकूलन
trick: Climate → getting used to the climate.
examples: Our focus was rest and acclimatization, but on day four the tests started.
Climbers need a few days of acclimatization before going higher.

usage.pattern: acclimatization to something (climate, altitude) · verb: acclimatize to something

meaning: Awards, praise or honours given for an achievement
trick: ACCOLADES ≈ 'a cola' for the champion — a reward for doing well.
examples: Despite all the money, the fans and the accolades, he still felt like a failure.
The film received accolades from critics around the world.

usage.pattern: receive/win accolades for something · accolades from someone

meaning: To adjust to fit someone's needs or wishes; also to provide room for someone
trick: Spelling: double C, double M — it accommodates two of each.
examples: It's unreasonable to expect two people to accommodate each other 100 percent.
The teacher tried to accommodate every student's needs.

usage.pattern: accommodate someone / someone's needs · accommodate each other

meaning: Went somewhere with someone; kept someone company
trick: Accompanied → company → kept someone's company.
examples: Jalil walked Mariam home in front of the villagers who accompanied them.
Her mother accompanied her to the interview.

usage.pattern: someone accompanied someone (to a place) · be accompanied by someone/something

meaning: A portable musical instrument with bellows that you squeeze and keys or buttons you press
trick: Accordion → it folds like an ACCORD (agreement) paper being squeezed in and out.
examples: Tariq's father sometimes played old Pashto songs on the accordion.
The accordion's sound filled the small café.

usage.pattern: play the accordion

meaning: Suggesting that you think someone has done something wrong
trick: Accusatory → accusation in your tone.
examples: His silence was broken only by an accusatory grunt.
She gave him an accusatory look when the cake went missing.

usage.pattern: an accusatory + look/tone/question

meaning: Showing that you think someone has done something wrong
hindi: आरोप लगाते हुए, दोष देते हुए
trick: Accusing → making an accusation.
examples: Like a compass needle that points north, a man's accusing finger always finds a woman.
She gave her brother an accusing look.

usage.pattern: an accusing + finger/look/voice · (verb) accuse someone of doing something

meaning: Familiar with something because it has happened often; used to it
trick: Accustomed → it has become your CUSTOM.
examples: I'm accustomed to sleeping alone.
Her eyes slowly grew accustomed to the dark.

usage.pattern: be/get accustomed to something / to doing something

meaning: Feeling a continuous, dull pain
trick: Ache + ing — 'ACHE' sounds like 'ek' pain that keeps going.
examples: I climb steadily from rock to rock, my leg muscles stretching and aching.
My legs were aching after the long hike.

usage.pattern: something is aching · an aching + body part

meaning: Doing something brilliantly; getting a top result
hindi: शानदार प्रदर्शन करते हुए, बाज़ी मारते हुए
trick: Ace → acing it: performing like an ace.
examples: Success may mean acing an exam or smashing a sales goal.
She is acing all her exams this year.

usage.pattern: acing a test/exam/interview

meaning: Accepting or admitting that something is true or exists; showing you have noticed someone
trick: Ac-KNOWLEDGE-ing — showing you have knowledge of it.
examples: Entitled people are incapable of acknowledging their own problems openly and honestly.
Acknowledging your mistakes is the first step to improving.

usage.pattern: acknowledge something / that ... · acknowledge someone (nod, smile)

meaning: Assistants who help a priest during a church service; also loyal followers of a leader
trick: Acolytes → 'a colleague' of the priest → helpers at the altar.
examples: With him were two acolytes, one of whom carried a censer.
Two acolytes lit the candles before the service began.

usage.pattern: a priest with his acolytes · acolytes of someone

meaning: A person you know slightly but who is not a close friend
trick: Jaan pehchaan wala — someone you know but not very well.
examples: He is a friend of a business acquaintance of your father's.
He's not a friend, just an acquaintance from college.

usage.pattern: an acquaintance of someone's · make someone's acquaintance

meaning: Officially declared not guilty of a crime
trick: Acquitted → 'QUIT it' → the court lets you quit the case, free of charges.
examples: Yes, you'll be acquitted, and we'll go swimming again on Sundays.
After two years, she was finally acquitted.

usage.pattern: be acquitted of a crime / charge

meaning: An area of land measured in acres
hindi: एकड़ में ज़मीन का क्षेत्रफल, रकबा
trick: Acreage → acre + age → how many acres you have.
examples: If one suggested sowing a bigger acreage with barley, the other demanded more oats.
The total acreage of the estate is huge.

usage.pattern: the acreage of something · large acreage

meaning: A short, well-known saying that expresses a general truth
trick: ADAGE ≈ 'AGE-old' saying — wisdom passed down through ages.
examples: As the old adage goes, the man who thinks he knows everything learns nothing.
He lived by the adage that honesty is the best policy.

usage.pattern: the (old) adage that ... · as the adage goes
partners: the adage that time is money

meaning: To follow a rule, plan or limit closely; also to stick firmly to a surface
trick: AD-HERE — glue it right 'here' so it sticks (like adhesive).
examples: It helps us understand and adhere to our own limits.
The sticker didn't adhere to the wet surface.

usage.pattern: adhere to something (rules, plan, surface)

meaning: A temporary pause or postponement of a meeting, trial, etc.
trick: Adjournment → a pause in the JOURNey; we'll continue later.
examples: The judge announced an adjournment till the afternoon.
After a short adjournment, the meeting resumed.

usage.pattern: an adjournment of something (meeting, trial) · ask for an adjournment

meaning: Warning or scolding someone firmly but gently
trick: Admonishing → 'ADD-MONISH' → like a teacher adding a warning; an admonishing look.
examples: Tariq's mother gave her husband an admonishing look.
She kept admonishing her son to drive carefully.

usage.pattern: admonish someone for (doing) something · an admonishing look

meaning: The period of life between childhood and adulthood; the teenage years
trick: ADOLESCENCE — the 'adult-essence' is still forming.
examples: For most of my adolescence, I dreamed of being a rock star.
Adolescence is a time of big physical and emotional change.

usage.pattern: during/in (someone's) adolescence

meaning: A hormone released in fear or excitement that makes the heart beat faster and gives a burst of energy
trick: Adrenaline rush — the energy boost you feel on a roller coaster.
examples: I can feel the adrenaline pumping through my body.
Skydiving gave her a huge rush of adrenaline.

usage.pattern: a rush/surge of adrenaline · adrenaline kicks in

meaning: Feeling lost, without purpose or direction; also (of a boat) floating without control
trick: A-DRIFT → drifting with no direction.
examples: For most of the days, Mariam stayed in bed, feeling adrift and forlorn.
After college he felt adrift, unsure what to do next.

usage.pattern: feel/be adrift · be cast adrift

meaning: Excessive admiration or praise
trick: ADULATION ≈ 'adore-lation' — adoring someone too much.
examples: It brought him a lot of attention and adulation.
The pop star enjoyed the adulation of millions of fans.

usage.pattern: the adulation of someone (fans, crowd)

meaning: A married person who has a sexual relationship with someone other than their spouse
hindi: व्यभिचारी, पराए से संबंध रखने वाला
trick: Adultery → the person who commits it is an adulterer.
examples: Ask an adulterer who lost her family whether pleasure made her happy.
She refused to forgive the adulterer who had betrayed her sister.

usage.pattern: an adulterer · be exposed as an adulterer

meaning: Sexual relationship between a married person and someone who is not their spouse
trick: Adultery → 'adult' + 'tery' — an adult cheating on their marriage.
examples: The new laws ordered women to cover and punished adultery with stoning.
The novel is about a marriage destroyed by adultery.

usage.pattern: commit adultery (with someone)

meaning: An unusual, exciting and sometimes risky experience or journey
trick: AD-VENTURE — 'venture' out into the unknown.
examples: Some people chase the thrill of a risky new adventure.
Their trip to the mountains was a real adventure.

usage.pattern: an adventure · go on an adventure · a sense of adventure

meaning: An opponent or enemy
trick: Adversary → 'ADVERSE' person → the one against you.
examples: Know the terrain, know yourself, and know your adversary in detail.
He defeated his old adversary in the final match.

usage.pattern: someone's adversary · an adversary of someone

meaning: Harmful or unfavourable; causing problems
trick: Adverse → 'ADD WORSE' → adds harm and trouble.
examples: Instead of recharging me, the long break had an adverse effect.
The medicine had no adverse effects.

usage.pattern: adverse + effect/conditions/weather · have an adverse effect on something

meaning: Difficulties, hardship or misfortune
trick: Adverse (add worse) → adversity: things keep getting worse.
examples: Adversity and failure are useful for developing strong-minded adults.
She showed great courage in the face of adversity.

usage.pattern: in the face of adversity · overcome adversity

meaning: A substance sprayed out of a can as a fine mist
trick: Aero (air) + sol → air spray.
examples: Each afternoon, I sprayed my stock with aerosol deodorizer.
She used an aerosol can to spray paint the wall.

usage.pattern: an aerosol (can/spray)

meaning: Badly affected by something painful, such as a disease or problem
trick: Afflicted by disease → a fly that afflicts you.
examples: Salamano's dog is ugly and afflicted with some skin disease.
He has been afflicted with back pain since the accident.

usage.pattern: be afflicted with/by something (disease, problem)

meaning: An action or remark that insults or hurts someone's dignity
trick: Affront → said right to your FRONT, to your face — an insult to your dignity.
examples: Packing up and running would be an even worse affront to her sons' sacrifice.
His rude comment was an affront to her pride.

usage.pattern: an affront to someone/something (dignity, pride)

meaning: Planned or thought about beforehand
trick: A-FORE-thought → thought before (as in 'malice aforethought').
examples: He was charged with murder of malice aforethought.
The jury decided the killing was done with malice aforethought.

usage.pattern: malice aforethought · with (malice) aforethought

meaning: The period or situation right after an event, and the mess or effects it leaves
hindi: बाद का असर, बाद की हालत
trick: After + math → the mess left after something happened.
examples: In the living room, she took in the aftermath of last night's Eid visits.
In the aftermath of the flood, many families were homeless.

usage.pattern: the aftermath of something · in the (immediate) aftermath of something
partners: in the aftermath of the war

meaning: To annoy or irritate someone (informal); also to make a problem worse
trick: Aggravate → 'aggro' → doing things to make someone aggro (angry).
examples: It's possible you hid it somewhere, just to aggravate me.
His constant humming really aggravates me.

usage.pattern: aggravate someone · aggravate a problem/injury

meaning: Gathering or grouping together into one mass or whole
hindi: इकट्ठा होते हुए, जमा होते हुए
trick: AGGREGATE ≈ 'a great gate' where everything gathers together.
examples: Below me, tourists were snapping photos and aggregating themselves into antlike groups.
People were aggregating near the gate, waiting for it to open.

usage.pattern: aggregate (themselves) into groups · aggregate data into something

meaning: Upset or angry because of unfair treatment
trick: A-GRIEVED → full of grief because of unfair treatment.
examples: She dreaded the confrontation, the aggrieved looks.
She felt aggrieved at being left out of the team.

usage.pattern: feel aggrieved (at/about something) · the aggrieved party

meaning: Able to move, think or adapt quickly and easily
trick: Agile → 'a GIRL' gymnast — quick to move, think and adapt.
examples: We can always become stronger and more agile, mentally and physically.
She has an agile mind and solves puzzles fast.

usage.pattern: an agile + person/animal/mind · be agile

meaning: Worried, nervous or angry and unable to stay calm
trick: Agitated → like a washing machine agitator, shaken up inside.
examples: When he was agitated, which happened often, his slurring got worse.
He became agitated when his phone went missing.

usage.pattern: be/get/become agitated (about/over something)

meaning: Worries or thinks very hard about something for a long time, with distress
hindi: बहुत परेशान होता है, तड़पता है
trick: Agony → agonizes: being in agony over a decision.
examples: He agonizes over every sign, every laugh, every smile.
She agonizes over every small decision.

usage.pattern: someone agonizes over/about something

meaning: Extreme physical or mental pain and suffering
trick: Agony → 'AGO-NY' → pain that won't go away.
examples: But the other side of being spared was the agony of wondering who hadn't.
He was in agony after breaking his leg.

usage.pattern: in agony · the agony of something

meaning: Help or support; to help
trick: First AID — help given immediately.
examples: Decisions based on emotion, without the aid of reason, usually go wrong.
A map will aid you in finding the way.

usage.pattern: with/without the aid of something · aid someone in (doing) something
partners: with the aid of a map

meaning: Troubled someone or caused them pain or illness
trick: "Ailed" sounds like "ill-ed" — was ill.
examples: No matter what ailed my body or my mind, I had the same solution.
Nobody knew what ailed the old dog.

usage.pattern: what ailed someone · something ailed someone

meaning: Illnesses, usually minor ones
trick: "Ail" = ill → ail-ments = illnesses.
examples: The ailments that would trouble Mammy for the rest of her days began.
Grandmother keeps home remedies for common ailments like colds and coughs.

usage.pattern: minor/common ailments · suffer from ailments

meaning: A particular feeling or quality that someone or something seems to have
trick: Like a smell in the air — a feeling around a person or place: air of eagerness, air of mystery.
examples: There was a faint smile on her lips, and an air of eagerness about her.
There was an air of mystery about the old house at the end of the street.

usage.pattern: an air of + quality (mystery, confidence) · have/give an air of something

meaning: A strip of ground where small aircraft can take off and land
trick: Air + strip = an air path on the ground.
examples: After the first week, we headed to an airstrip in Yuma to start jumping.
The small plane landed on a dusty airstrip near the village.

usage.pattern: land on / take off from an airstrip

meaning: Vague, impractical and not based on reality
trick: Made of AIR and FAIRY dust — nothing solid or practical.
examples: No, not that airy-fairy, eternal bliss kind of enlightenment.
We need real figures, not airy-fairy ideas.

usage.pattern: airy-fairy + ideas/plans · be a bit airy-fairy

meaning: A passage between rows of seats or shelves
hindi: गलियारा, कतारों के बीच का रास्ता
trick: Think of the aisle seat on a plane or the aisles in a supermarket.
examples: She made her way down the aisle to the back of the bus.
I always book an aisle seat so I can stretch my legs.

usage.pattern: in/down the aisle · an aisle seat

meaning: Similar to; of a similar kind
trick: AKIN ≈ 'a kin' (family) — related, so similar.
examples: For a teenage nerd like me, it was akin to winning the lottery.
The feeling was akin to falling in love.

usage.pattern: be akin to something / to doing something

meaning: Although; even though
trick: ALBEIT = 'ALl BE IT' so — although it is so.
examples: I became an immature, selfish, albeit sometimes charming player.
He agreed, albeit reluctantly.

usage.pattern: ..., albeit + adjective/adverb/noun phrase (= although)

meaning: A tree or shrub of the birch family that grows in wet ground
trick: Alder bushes grow "older" near rivers and wet land.
examples: They went for walks among the fallen leaves and alder bushes.
The riverbank was lined with tall alder trees.

usage.pattern: an alder (tree) · alder + noun

meaning: A type of beer; in 'ginger ale', a sweet fizzy ginger soft drink
hindi: एक प्रकार की बीयर; अदरक वाला ठंडा पेय
trick: Ale = beer; also think of ginger ale.
examples: They sit on a blanket and drink cold ginger ale.
The travellers drank ale at the village inn.

usage.pattern: a glass of (ginger) ale

meaning: A plant grown as food for farm animals
trick: "Alfalfa" — food for the animal farm.
examples: Babi said the fields were green winter wheat and alfalfa.
The farmer fed his cows fresh alfalfa every morning.

usage.pattern: alfalfa (for animals) · alfalfa + noun

meaning: Making someone feel isolated, unwelcome or unfriendly towards you
hindi: अलग-थलग करते हुए, दूर करते हुए
trick: ALIEN-ating — making someone feel like an alien among you.
examples: I was drinking far too much and alienating a number of friends.
The new policy risks alienating loyal customers.

usage.pattern: alienate someone (from someone/something) · an alienating experience

meaning: Money that a person is legally ordered to pay to their former spouse after divorce
trick: ALI-MONEY — the money paid after the marriage ends.
examples: The lawyers go home and the alimony check is in the mail.
The court ordered him to pay monthly alimony.

usage.pattern: pay alimony (to someone) · receive alimony

meaning: Reduced or calmed fears, worries or doubts
trick: "All-ayed" = "all okay" — makes the worry go away.
examples: Her anxieties that their life together is only temporary are allayed.
The doctor's calm words allayed her fears about the surgery.

usage.pattern: allay someone's fears/doubts/worries

meaning: To make pain, suffering or a problem less severe
trick: ALLEVIATE ≈ 'all elevate' — lift all the weight off and make it lighter.
examples: We like the idea that we can alleviate all our suffering permanently.
The medicine helped alleviate her headache.

usage.pattern: alleviate pain/suffering/a problem

meaning: Very attractive or tempting in a mysterious way
trick: A LURE — a fishing lure attracts and tempts the fish.
examples: This confidence can be alluring to others, at least for a while.
She found the offer of a job abroad very alluring.

usage.pattern: an alluring + smell/offer/person · find something alluring

meaning: Keeping apart from others and not taking part; also cold and unfriendly
trick: A-loof ≈ alone — someone who stays apart from others.
examples: Only Napoleon held aloof.
She remained aloof from the office gossip.

usage.pattern: hold/remain/stay aloof (from someone/something)

meaning: The quality of being distant and unfriendly
trick: Aloof (alone, unfriendly) + -ness = the state of being aloof.
examples: All those years of aloofness, of cooping herself up and not caring.
His aloofness made it hard for new classmates to approach him.

usage.pattern: someone's aloofness · an air of aloofness

meaning: Arranged in the order of the alphabet
trick: Alphabet + -ized = put in A-B-C order.
examples: She took down Babi's books, dusted and alphabetized them.
All the files were neatly alphabetized in the cabinet.

usage.pattern: alphabetize a list/files · an alphabetized list

meaning: An instrument that measures altitude (height above sea level)
trick: Alti-meter = altitude meter.
examples: On my first high jump, I couldn't take my eyes off my altimeter.
The pilot checked the altimeter before descending.

usage.pattern: the altimeter reads/shows + height

meaning: Tiny air sacs in the lungs where oxygen enters the blood
trick: Alveoli = "air valley" — tiny air pockets in the lungs.
examples: His alveoli, or air sacs, were filling with fluid.
Oxygen passes from the alveoli into the bloodstream.

usage.pattern: the alveoli (in the lungs)

meaning: A warm yellowish-orange color (also the hardened tree resin of that color)
trick: Amber is the color of the middle traffic light.
examples: The amber tip of his cigarette brightened and dimmed.
The traffic light turned amber, so he slowed down.

usage.pattern: amber + noun (light, eyes) · in amber

meaning: Walked slowly and in a relaxed way
trick: "Amble" sounds like "ramble" — a slow, easy walk.
examples: When it was too cold to go outside, Laila ambled around the house.
We ambled along the beach after dinner.

usage.pattern: someone ambled + along/around/to a place

meaning: A surprise attack by people who were hiding
trick: Am-BUSH — attackers hiding in the bush.
examples: The horses and cows had been lying in ambush in the cowshed.
The soldiers were caught in an ambush on the mountain road.

usage.pattern: ambush someone; be ambushed by someone; lie in ambush

meaning: (in 'make amends') something done to make up for a wrong or hurt you caused
trick: Amends → MEND → mend things after you hurt someone.
examples: Sometimes he would try to make amends for the slaps with empty apologies.
He tried to make amends for his rude behaviour by apologising.

usage.pattern: make amends (to someone) for something / for doing something

meaning: Friendly and pleasant
trick: "Am I able to be friendly?" — yes, amiable = friendly.
examples: Her friend stood at the door with his white beard and amiable, toothless smile.
They had an amiable chat over tea.

usage.pattern: be amiable; an amiable person / chat

meaning: In a friendly and pleasant way
trick: Amiable (friendly) + -ly = in a friendly way.
examples: Mariam waved amiably.
The two old rivals chatted amiably at the reunion.

usage.pattern: talk / smile / chat amiably (with someone)

meaning: A friend (informal, from Spanish)
trick: Spanish for friend — 'Hola, amigo!'
examples: Calm down, amigo.
He greeted me with a smile: 'Hello, amigo!'

usage.pattern: my amigo; Hello, amigo!

meaning: Facts or weaknesses that someone can use against you; also bullets and shells fired from guns
hindi: किसी के ख़िलाफ़ इस्तेमाल होने वाली बात; गोला-बारूद
trick: Ammo-nition = bullets and bombs.
examples: I was showing a ton of weakness, which gave Gary ammunition.
His mistakes gave his opponents ammunition to criticise him.

usage.pattern: give someone ammunition (against someone) · ammunition for something

meaning: To make something more intense or exciting; to hype up
trick: Amp = amplifier — turn the volume and energy up.
examples: A competitive environment can amp up an entire platoon's commitment.
The DJ amped up the music as midnight approached.

usage.pattern: amp up something / amp something up

meaning: Done on both land and water (of military operations or vehicles); also an animal like a frog that lives on land and in water
trick: Amphi = both → works on both land and water.
examples: Both skills come in handy on amphibian operations.
A frog is an amphibian that starts life in water.

usage.pattern: amphibian + operation/vehicle · an amphibian (animal)

meaning: More than enough
trick: Ample = A-plenty — more than enough.
examples: Mariam would have ample occasion to think about how things might have turned out.
You will have ample time to finish the test.

usage.pattern: ample time / space / evidence (to do something)

meaning: Makes something louder, bigger or stronger
trick: Amplify your voice — a microphone amplifies sound.
examples: A spin cycle of panic and doubt only amplifies your self-torture.
Social media often amplifies rumours.

usage.pattern: something amplifies a sound / a feeling / a problem

meaning: Cut off (a limb) by surgery
trick: Andrew Tate - hair cut — a cut, but of limbs, done surgically.
examples: Finish the race strong and worry about amputated toes at the hospital later.
Her frostbitten fingers had to be amputated.

usage.pattern: someone's leg / arm was amputated

meaning: The surgical cutting off of a limb
trick: Amputate (Andrew Tate - cut) + -ion = the process of cutting off a limb.
examples: Tariq told her the bone spurs sometimes grew after an amputation.
The infection was so severe that amputation was the only option.

usage.pattern: an amputation of a leg / arm; need an amputation

meaning: A person who has had a limb amputated
hindi: जिसका अंग कटा हो, अपंग व्यक्ति
trick: Amputate + -ee = the person it was done to (like employee).
examples: The ache of his absence was like the phantom pain of an amputee.
The amputee ran the marathon on a prosthetic leg.

usage.pattern: an amputee (a person who has lost a limb)

meaning: To entertain someone or make them laugh or smile
trick: "A music" — something that entertains you.
examples: I keep things that amuse me from the papers in an album.
The clown's tricks never fail to amuse the children.

usage.pattern: amuse someone; amuse yourself by doing something

meaning: Believing in a society with no government and no private property, where everything is shared; also a person with these beliefs
trick: ANARCHY (no government) + COMMUNIST (shared property).
examples: If my goal was to become an anarcho-communist revolutionary, my failure to make money was a success.
He described himself as an anarcho-communist in his youth.

usage.pattern: an anarcho-communist + noun; be an anarcho-communist

meaning: Fixed firmly and deeply in something (such as the mind); also held in place by an anchor
hindi: गहराई से बैठा, जमा हुआ; लंगर डाला
trick: A ship anchored deep cannot drift.
examples: Those moments were anchored deep in my subconscious.
Her beliefs are anchored in her family values.

usage.pattern: be anchored in / to something

meaning: A doctor who gives anesthesia so patients feel no pain during surgery
trick: Anesthesia + -ologist = the doctor who handles anesthesia.
examples: The anesthesiologist placed an oxygen mask over my face and counted down softly.
Before surgery, the anesthesiologist explained how she would be put to sleep.

usage.pattern: the anesthesiologist puts the patient to sleep before surgery

meaning: A drug that stops you feeling pain
hindi: बेहोशी की दवा, सुन्न करने वाली दवा
trick: An-esthetic = no feeling — the drug that numbs pain.
examples: Regina loaded a syringe with local anesthetic for the wound on my hand.
The dentist gave him a local anesthetic before pulling the tooth.

usage.pattern: give someone an anesthetic; under (general / local) anesthetic

meaning: Full of anxiety, worry or teenage-style emotional turmoil
trick: ANGST (German for fear/anxiety) + y — moody and anxious.
examples: Josh and I sat in the pool, drinking beers and talking as young angsty males do.
He went through an angsty phase in high school.

usage.pattern: be / feel angsty; an angsty teenager / song

meaning: Severe mental or emotional suffering
trick: Anguish sounds like "anger + languish" — deep emotional suffering.
examples: I chose physical pain now over the mental anguish of regret later.
The mother cried out in anguish when she heard the news.

usage.pattern: be in anguish; anguish over / at something

meaning: Wild, funny or silly behaviour that gets attention
trick: Ant-ics — like ants running around in silly ways.
examples: My antics annoyed the instructors and fired up my crew.
The children laughed at the clown's antics.

usage.pattern: someone's antics; the antics of someone

meaning: A heavy iron block on which a blacksmith hammers metal; (figurative) a hard, crushing test
trick: Anvil — where iron gets hammered; under the anvil, the weak crumble.
examples: Many great athletes crumbled beneath the anvil of ultra running.
The blacksmith hammered the red-hot iron on the anvil.

usage.pattern: hammer metal on an anvil; beneath the anvil of something (figurative)

meaning: Into separate pieces; also separated by distance or time
trick: A-PART = into parts, separated.
examples: His body was limp, so he didn't come apart when he hit the ground.
The old chair fell apart when he sat on it.

usage.pattern: come / fall / break apart; take something apart; live apart

meaning: A lack of interest, enthusiasm or concern
trick: A-pathy = no feeling — "I don't care."
examples: At the beginning they met with much stupidity and apathy.
Voter apathy led to a very low turnout.

usage.pattern: apathy towards / about something

meaning: A machine or set of equipment made for a particular job
trick: "A pair of us" — a set of tools working together.
examples: The condemned man had to hope the apparatus was in good working order!
Firefighters wear breathing apparatus in smoky buildings.

usage.pattern: an apparatus for doing something; the apparatus works / fails

meaning: Clearly seen or understood; also seeming real but possibly not
trick: Spelling: A-PP-A-RENT — it's 'a parent' that is clearly visible, not 'apparant'.
examples: The tendency toward entitlement is apparent across all of society.
It was apparent that she was tired.

usage.pattern: It is apparent that...; for no apparent reason

meaning: A ghostly or unreal image of a person; something seen that is not really there
trick: Apparition = something that suddenly appears — the spirit of a dead person.
examples: She wanted to prove he was really here, not a dream, an apparition.
She claimed to have seen an apparition in the old castle.

usage.pattern: an apparition appears / of someone

meaning: To calm or please someone by giving them what they want
trick: Ap-PEASE ≈ please — make them happy/calm.
examples: Everything she did was an effort to appease him so he wouldn't beat her sons.
The manager offered a refund to appease the angry customer.

usage.pattern: appease someone (by doing something)

meaning: The act of calming or satisfying someone (even your own conscience); also giving in to demands to keep the peace
trick: Appease (please) + -ment = making someone (or yourself) feel calm.
examples: His gestures were meant more for his own appeasement than hers.
The policy of appeasement failed to prevent the war.

usage.pattern: for someone's appeasement; a policy of appeasement

meaning: Looking or smelling good enough to make you hungry
hindi: स्वादिष्ट दिखने वाला, भूख जगाने वाला
trick: Appetite + -ising = it raises your appetite (appetizing food).
examples: A warm, rich, appetising scent wafted across the yard.
The bakery had an appetising smell of fresh bread.

usage.pattern: something looks / smells appetising

meaning: Worry or fear that something bad will happen
trick: Apprehension = worry about the future.
examples: Tariq's face showed apprehension, tenderness and embarrassment.
She felt a sense of apprehension before her first job interview.

usage.pattern: apprehension about / over something; with apprehension

meaning: Worried or nervous that something bad will happen
trick: Apprehensive = feeling apprehension — worried about the future.
examples: Zalmai only sucked his thumb when he was apprehensive.
He was apprehensive about flying for the first time.

usage.pattern: be / feel apprehensive about something / about doing something

meaning: Suitable or correct for the situation; the right one needed
trick: AP-PROPER-iate — the proper thing for the occasion.
examples: Filling out the appropriate paperwork to drop out of med school is easy.
Jeans are not appropriate for a job interview.

usage.pattern: the appropriate + noun; appropriate for something

meaning: Small, soft, orange-yellow fruits with a stone inside
trick: Apri-cots — a fruit that looks like a tiny peach.
examples: Laila dipped a spoon into her bowl of soaked raisins, pistachios, and apricots.
She bought a bag of dried apricots for the trip.

usage.pattern: dried / fresh apricots

meaning: Pieces of cloth worn over the front of clothes to keep them clean, e.g. while cooking
trick: Aprons — what you wear while cooking.
examples: Nearly all the women wore aprons tied tight round their waists.
The chefs tied on their aprons before the dinner rush.

usage.pattern: wear / put on / tie aprons

meaning: Likely to; having a natural tendency to
hindi: आदत होना, प्रवृत्ति होना, संभावना होना
trick: Apt to = like to — "he is apt to forget" = he tends to forget.
examples: He is apt to lose his temper when he is tired.
Young children are apt to put things in their mouths.

usage.pattern: someone / something is apt to do something

meaning: A glass tank or building where fish and other water animals are kept
trick: Aqua = water → a fish tank.
examples: I was a lone fish in a glass box aquarium under hot show lights.
He cleans the aquarium in his bedroom every Sunday.

usage.pattern: keep fish in an aquarium; visit an aquarium

meaning: Based on random choice or personal whim rather than reason or a system
trick: ARBITRARY ≈ 'a bit random' — no real reason behind it.
examples: Not many people want to suffer through arbitrary corporate hierarchies.
The rules seemed arbitrary and unfair.

usage.pattern: an arbitrary decision / rule / choice

meaning: A curved line or shape, like part of a circle
trick: Think of a rainbow — it forms an arc across the sky.
examples: A paper airplane floats across the room in a high arc.
A rainbow stretched in a perfect arc over the hills.

usage.pattern: in an arc; the arc of something

meaning: Without a curve or arch (e.g. straight, flat eyebrows or flat feet)
trick: Arch + less = no curve.
examples: Mariam saw her own face, the archless, unshapely eyebrows and the flat hair.
She drew curves on her archless eyebrows with a pencil.

usage.pattern: archless eyebrows / feet

meaning: Very difficult and tiring; needing a lot of effort
trick: 'ARD-uous' sounds like 'HARD-uous' → hard, challenging.
examples: These activities are stressful, arduous, and often unpleasant.
Preparing for the exam was an arduous task.

usage.pattern: an arduous journey / task / climb

meaning: The highest social class, usually people of noble birth with titles and wealth
trick: Aristocrats = upper-class people (lords, dukes, nobles).
examples: The era of aristocracy, nepotism, and inequality is over.
Before the revolution, the aristocracy owned most of the land.

usage.pattern: the aristocracy; a member of the aristocracy

meaning: Came into existence or appeared (past tense of arise); got up
trick: A ROSE arose from the ground — it came up.
examples: Her story makes sense when we understand the values in which her beliefs arose.
A problem arose during the meeting.

usage.pattern: a problem / question / chance arose (from something)

meaning: Without a regular rhythm; irregular in beat
trick: A (not) + rhythmic → irregular rhythm.
examples: It looked like an arrhythmic EKG.
The patient's arrhythmic heartbeat worried the doctors.

usage.pattern: an arrhythmic heartbeat / beat

meaning: A blood vessel that carries blood away from the heart to the body
trick: Like a vein, but an ARTery goes Away from the heart.
examples: Out the words came, like blood gushing from an artery.
A blocked artery can cause a heart attack.

usage.pattern: a blocked / main artery; an artery carries blood from the heart

meaning: Affected by arthritis; having swollen, painful, stiff joints
trick: Arthritis → arthritic joints are swollen.
examples: He tapped her cheek with one arthritic finger.
Her arthritic fingers made it hard to open jars.

usage.pattern: arthritic knees / hands / joints

meaning: To express a thought or feeling clearly in words; also (adjective) able to speak clearly
hindi: शब्दों में कहना, साफ़-साफ़ कहना; स्पष्ट बोलने वाला
trick: 'Art' of speaking → put feelings into clear words.
examples: If she could articulate it, she might have said she was tired of being used.
He struggled to articulate his feelings.

usage.pattern: articulate something (a feeling / an idea / a thought)

meaning: Large, heavy guns, often mounted on wheels, used in war
trick: ART-ILLERY → guns on wheels that make things 'ill'.
examples: Outside, there was the far-off boom of artillery, then gunfire.
The artillery fired at the enemy positions all night.

usage.pattern: artillery fire; heavy artillery

meaning: The act of climbing or moving upward
trick: Ascent and descent — ascent goes UP (A for Above).
examples: Each lap demanded an ascent and descent of around 5,000 vertical feet.
The ascent to the top of the mountain took six hours.

usage.pattern: the ascent of a mountain; make the ascent

meaning: Very pale or grey, like ash (often from shock or illness)
trick: Ash-en → grey like ash.
examples: Their faces were ashen gray after the long, uneasy vigil.
His face turned ashen when he heard the news.

usage.pattern: someone's face turned / went ashen

meaning: Attacking or insulting someone's reputation with false or damaging claims
hindi: बदनाम करते हुए, लांछन लगाते हुए
trick: Aspersing → 'a spray' of insults on someone's name.
examples: Does my friend think that by aspersing a witness he will shake the evidence?
Stop aspersing her reputation without any proof.

usage.pattern: by aspersing someone; aspersing someone's character / reputation

meaning: A black, sticky material used for making roads (tar)
trick: Asphalt = 'damber' (tar) on the road.
examples: My favorite run was an asphalt path that wound through the trees.
The workers spread fresh asphalt on the road.

usage.pattern: lay asphalt; an asphalt road

meaning: Judged or measured (past participle of assess)
trick: Assess — like an exam that tests and grades you.
examples: The values, and the metrics by which those values are assessed, stay the same.
Students are assessed at the end of each term.

usage.pattern: something is assessed by / on something; someone assessed something

meaning: Collections of different kinds of things mixed together
hindi: तरह-तरह की चीज़ों के संग्रह, मिश्रण
trick: Assortment of vegetables → different types sorted together.
examples: Other times, she met with assortments of wooden clubs, short whips and slaps.
The shop sells assortments of chocolates for gifts.

usage.pattern: an assortment of something (sweets / colours / vegetables)

meaning: Promises or statements meant to remove doubt and give confidence
trick: To assure → give assurances.
examples: She could now hear the hollow, false assurances clearly.
Despite his assurances, the work was not finished on time.

usage.pattern: give / receive assurances (that...)

meaning: Greatly surprised or amazed
trick: Astonished = so surprised you turn to STONE.
examples: Laila is astonished that she too has survived.
She was astonished to see her old friend at the door.

usage.pattern: be astonished at / by something; astonished to see / hear

meaning: Extremely surprising or impressive
trick: So surprising it turns you to STONE.
examples: It's astonishing I even made it through Hell Week.
The child showed an astonishing talent for music.

usage.pattern: It is astonishing that...; an astonishing result / speed

meaning: A feeling of great surprise
trick: Astonish + ment → the feeling of being stunned like stone.
examples: To her astonishment, Rasheed calmly walked out of the room.
He stared at the results in astonishment.

usage.pattern: in astonishment; to someone's astonishment

meaning: Shocked and very surprised
trick: Astounded = struck by a loud SOUND of shock.
examples: She was too astounded to notice what her hand had done.
We were astounded by the size of the crowd.

usage.pattern: be astounded by / at something; astounded to learn

meaning: Away from the right path; into wrong thinking or behaviour
trick: A stray dog wanders astray — off the right path.
examples: No argument must lead you astray.
Bad friends can lead you astray.

usage.pattern: go astray; lead someone astray

meaning: With one leg on each side of something
trick: A + stride → legs spread across, one on each side.
examples: The tobacconist sat astride a chair, resting his arms on the back.
He sat astride the horse.

usage.pattern: sit astride something (a horse / bike / wall)

meaning: Across, from side to side (often in the way)
trick: A-THWART → lying across your path, thwarting you.
examples: The Arab drew his knife and held it up toward me, athwart the sunlight.
A fallen tree lay athwart the road.

usage.pattern: athwart something (across it)

meaning: On the top of
trick: A + top → on top of.
examples: She spotted a pack of cigarettes atop the dresser.
A small bird sat atop the flagpole.

usage.pattern: atop something (on top of it)

meaning: Possible to achieve or reach
hindi: प्राप्त करने योग्य, हासिल होने लायक
trick: Possible to attain → attain + able.
examples: Our imagination hunts down dreams that suddenly feel attainable.
Set goals that are challenging but attainable.

usage.pattern: an attainable goal / target; attainable for someone

meaning: Tried to do something, often something difficult
trick: AT-TEMPT-ed — tempted to try, so you attempted it.
examples: He was a failure at everything he had attempted.
He attempted to climb the mountain alone.

usage.pattern: someone attempted (to do) something

meaning: A traditional Afghan soup with noodles, vegetables and yogurt
trick: Aush sounds like 'ash-soup' → a warm Afghan noodle soup.
examples: Babi dipped bread into his bowl of aush.
Her mother made a pot of aush for dinner.

usage.pattern: a bowl of aush; make / eat aush

meaning: The freedom to govern yourself or make your own decisions without outside control
trick: AUTO (self) + NOMY (law) — making your own laws, like an automatic self-driving car.
examples: It was freedom, autonomy.
Teenagers often want more autonomy over their lives.

usage.pattern: autonomy over / in something; give someone autonomy

meaning: A close review of what went wrong, like a doctor examining a body; also a medical examination of a dead body to find the cause of death
trick: Auto (self) + opsy (see) → see for yourself why it died or failed.
examples: A tactical review is the most vital piece of any live autopsy.
The autopsy showed that he died of a heart attack.

usage.pattern: do an autopsy on something (a failure / a body)

meaning: The season between summer and winter, when leaves fall
trick: Autumn = the season when leaves fall (fall).
examples: By the autumn the animals were tired but happy.
The trees turn red and gold in autumn.

usage.pattern: in autumn; autumn leaves

meaning: A group that helps or supports a main organisation; also (adjective) extra, backup
trick: Auxiliary → the helping/support team.
examples: I joined the Civil Air Patrol, the civilian auxiliary of the Air Force.
The ship has an auxiliary engine in case the main one fails.

usage.pattern: an auxiliary of something; auxiliary + noun (staff / power)

meaning: A strong feeling of dislike
trick: A-VERSION you hate → strong dislike.
examples: The first step is to get over your aversion to negotiating.
He has a strong aversion to spicy food.

usage.pattern: an aversion to something / to doing something

meaning: Turned away (your eyes or face); also prevented something bad from happening
trick: Averted eyes = AVOIDED looking.
examples: Some averted their eyes, almost embarrassed.
Quick thinking averted a serious accident.

usage.pattern: avert your eyes / gaze; avert a crisis

meaning: Pilots; people who fly aircraft
trick: Aviation → aviate → aviators are pilots.
examples: A quick reaction force of Navy SEALs, marines, and aviators was assembled.
The aviators prepared their planes for the air show.

usage.pattern: aviators fly planes; aviator sunglasses

meaning: Extremely eager and interested; enthusiastic
trick: Avid reader → can't wait to read more.
examples: The most avid was Naghma, who followed Mariam everywhere.
She is an avid reader who finishes a book every week.

usage.pattern: an avid reader / fan; the most avid

meaning: Covered or flooded with something (light, water); also having too much of something
trick: The floor was awash → washed all over with water.
examples: Mariam saw tulips and lilies, their petals awash in sunlight.
After the pipe burst, the floor was awash with water.

usage.pattern: be awash in / with something

meaning: A feeling of great respect mixed with wonder or fear
trick: 'Awww!' — the sound you make in wonder, respect, or surprise.
examples: A woman sitting near him was looking on in awe.
They stood in awe of the giant waterfall.

usage.pattern: in awe of someone / something; stare in awe

meaning: Filled with a feeling of wonder, admiration and respect
trick: Struck by awe → awestruck.
examples: The women eyed her with a reverent, almost awestruck, expression.
The children were awestruck by the fireworks.

usage.pattern: be awestruck by something

meaning: Very bad or unpleasant
trick: AW-ful — 'aww' full of disappointment; very bad.
examples: This value gave him awful problems, like needing to sell more records.
The weather was awful all weekend.

usage.pattern: awful + noun; feel awful (about something)

meaning: For a short time
trick: A while → for some time.
examples: She went back to the stream and waited awhile longer.
Sit down and rest awhile.

usage.pattern: stay / wait / rest awhile

meaning: A sheet of cloth or other material over a door or window to give shade or shelter
trick: An awning protects you from the sun's 'dawning' rays.
examples: They ate beneath the awning of a closed rug shop.
We stood under the shop's awning to avoid the rain.

usage.pattern: under an awning; an awning over a door / window
